subject: Dedicated capacity — acceptance sampling & binding-rate agreement
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — acceptance sampling & binding-rate agreement

Hi Sara,

Following up from our call last week — attached is a concise proposal for how Redwood would validate the Dedicated commit (GPU pool sizing + throughput guarantee) so we can finalize pricing/discount bands. High-level notes:

- What we measure: sustained tokens/sec (server-side emitted tokens) and requests/sec for short-completion workflows. We also sample latency (p50/p95/p99) at the model-output boundary.
- Measurement windows: we propose two steady-state runs (1 hour each) with a 10-minute warm-up. Tokens/sec should be computed over a 5-minute sliding window.
- Acceptance criteria: performance bands in the attached spreadsheet. Examples: baseline target = 120k tokens/sec aggregate across the pool; p95 output latency <= 200ms for warm requests.
- Test traffic: a replay of production-sampled traces + a synthetic tail set to stress batch and KV-cache locality.
- Ramp and cold starts: we’ll run a separate cold-start check (30 concurrent cold requests) and include warm-up allowance for autoscaler.

Asks: please confirm the following so we can lock the commercial paperwork:
1) Window you want the test to run (we suggested Tue 22 Jun or Wed 23 Jun).
2) Whether you accept the replay-based traces (we can also work from an anonymized production sample you provide).
3) Headroom for autoscaler and whether burst capacity will be included in the commit.

I’ve cc’d Ben and Karthik — Ben will propose the discount bands tied to commit length and performance warranty; Karthik is our validation lead and will own the runbook. I attached a short acceptance-criteria workbook and the benchmark script we’ll run.

If we can align by Wednesday, we’ll flip the PO and apply the proposed commit discounts.

Thanks,

— Tessa

Thanks Tessa — appreciate the clear framework. A few quick questions from our side before we lock dates:

- Production traces: we prefer Redwood to run replay with an anonymized sample we provide (contains multi-model fanout and per-request prompt length distribution). Can you confirm the replay tooling preserves token boundaries and batching semantics?
- Cold-starts: our primary concern is bursty nightly jobs; we need a clear measurement for single-request latency when the KV cache is not populated.
- Measurement fairness: we need to ensure spikes from downstream (our inference coordinators) are not counted against Redwood — can we add application-level markers to exclude known scheduled spikes?
- Commercial: procurement is asking for a 12-month commit with a performance SLA and a 30% discount floor for the first year if the baseline throughput is met. They also want the credit formula (if we miss targets) incorporated into the MSA.

We can do Tue 29 Jun for a test window if that works on your side (gives us time to produce the anonymized traces).

-Sara

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sara Lam <sara.lam@polarishealthtech.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — acceptance sampling & binding-rate agreement

Sara — thanks for the questions. Below are concrete defs and a proposed commercial mapping so procurement has something to review:

Measurement definitions (technical)
- "Tokens/sec": measured at the model output (server-side emit). We use a 5-minute sliding window, sampled every 30s. Sustained throughput = median of windowed averages across the run.
- "Requests/sec": counted at request completion. For short completions (< 512 tokens) we use requests/sec as the primary metric; for long generations tokens/sec is primary.
- Latency: we capture p50/p95/p99 on model emit time (excluding network deserialization); warm-run p95 <= 200ms target, cold-start p95 <= 500ms.
- Acceptance run strategy: two independent 1-hour steady-state runs (10-minute warm-up each). A pass requires meeting throughput target on both runs (>= target tokens/sec in >= 95% of 5-minute windows).
- Replays vs synthetic: we strongly prefer production-sampled replays for realism, with a synthetic tail to exercise batching and KV-cache misses. Redwood will supply the replay harness; Polaris provides trace sample.

Commercial mapping (proposal)
- Commit bands: 3-month reserved commit -> 15% list discount; 12-month reserved commit -> 25% list discount (applies to compute base rate).
- Performance warranty: if throughput falls short of the agreed baseline during acceptance or live 30-day ramp, Redwood issues credits: 1% of monthly invoice per 1% shortfall, up to a cap. Proposal: cap = 30% of monthly invoice. (We are open to limited-term exceptions in early months.)
- Ramp & burst: during the 30-day ramp period Redwood will allow a 15% headroom for autoscaler migration. Bursts that exceed that and cause measurable degradation will be excluded if proactively flagged by Polaris via the application marker method.
- Test window: Ben suggests Tue 29 Jun for the first replay run and Wed 30 Jun as the fall-back. Karthik will own the runbook and upload logs to the Jira ticket INF-762.

Operational asks
- Polaris to provide anonymized sample trace (S3 link) 4 days before test window.
- Polaris to confirm whether burst capacity is included in billable commit (this affects pool sizing + discount).

I’ll put the proposed credit formula and a worked example into a short PDF and attach to the deal record.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference.com

Sara/Team — thanks for the quick turn. Short summary and adjustments so procurement can review a single doc: 

- Test date: target Tue 29 Jun (Polaris to upload anonymized trace to S3 by Fri 25 Jun).
- Acceptance: two 1-hour steady-state runs with 10-minute warm-up; pass requires >= baseline tokens/sec in >= 95% of 5-min windows across both runs.
- Cold-start check: separate 30-request cold-start probe; p95 <= 500ms.
- Credits: Redwood proposal = 1% invoice credit per 1% throughput shortfall, capped at 30% of monthly invoice. We will mark scheduled maintenance and flagged application spikes as excluded events.
- Commercial: 12-month reserved commit -> 25% discount (applies if acceptance pass and PO signed). Procurement asked for a 30% floor — we can discuss an incremental rebate structure during QBRs but can’t increase the immediate discount above 25% without additional margin commitments.

I attached a cleaned acceptance-criteria workbook and a short commit summary for the procurement packet (includes example credit calc). If that looks good, Ben will prep the MSA language for the performance warranty and I’ll route the PO and DocuSign.

Requested next steps:
1) Polaris: confirm S3 trace link by end of day Fri 25 Jun.
2) Redwood: Ben to share the example credit calc PDF in HubSpot and Karthik to finalize the runbook in INF-762.
3) Procurement: let us know whether burst capacity should be counted toward the reserved commit.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this up.

— Tessa
